mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through lower cost of capital for corporate investment.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in the low-FEDFUNDS regime (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) are not significantly higher than in the high-FEDFUNDS regime (FEDFUNDS >= 0.5%) (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.5% signals weak labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, directly causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 5.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in consumer credit demand (RSAFS) and rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals reduced credit availability and higher borrowing costs, suppressing consumer spending and corporate investment to drive negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS declines and FEDFUNDS rises (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During post-recession recovery, rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strengthening manufacturing output that boosts corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of rising INDPRO (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising residential construction permits (HOUST) signals expanding housing market activity that increases consumer wealth and spending, directly producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST rises (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate exceeding 0.5% signals monetary tightening that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Overheating labor market (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly) combined with declining consumer credit demand (RSAFS) indicates labor-demand mismatch that reduces consumer spending and drives negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and RSAFS declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In high labor market tightness (UNRATE < 5.0%), strong payroll growth (PAYEMS) supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during high labor market tightness (UNRATE < 5.0%) with PAYEMS growth > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).
